assignment.description:
🔬 The Paranoid Style — Welcome to the Apocalypse

Text-only assignment • Total Points: 200

Lesson Notebook:
📎 Link: Open the Jupyter Book lesson

📌 Instructions

Answer each question in 3–5 complete sentences. Draw directly from the lesson content (and audio), but write in your own words. Cite any outside sources you use.

  1. Defining the Style: In your own words, what does Hofstadter mean by the “paranoid style” in American politics? How is it different from simply believing your side is right?
  2. Historical Case Study: Choose one of Hofstadter’s examples (such as the Anti-Masons, anti-Catholic movements, Populists, or anti-Communists). Explain how that movement shows the paranoid style at work.
  3. Democracy and Institutions: According to the lesson, how can the paranoid style weaken trust in democratic institutions like elections, courts, or the press?
  4. Modern Connection: Describe a contemporary situation (from any part of the political spectrum) where you see similar patterns of apocalyptic or conspiratorial thinking. How does Hofstadter’s framework help you understand it?

📂 Submission

Type your answers directly into the Canvas text box.

✅ Grading

  • Total Points: 200
  • Evaluated for accuracy, use of lesson evidence, clarity, and completeness.
  • You must score at least 134/200 across the module’s required work to unlock the next module.

⚖ Academic Integrity

There is no need to use AI tools to complete this lesson. You may use AI to help you format or polish your writing, but the ideas, analysis, and examples you submit must be entirely your own. Submitting AI-generated answers as your own work is considered academic dishonesty.

💡 Tips for Success

  • Reference specific examples from Hofstadter’s essay and from the lesson notes.
  • Use complete sentences and explain your reasoning clearly.
  • Define key terms the first time you use them (e.g., paranoid style, apocalyptic rhetoric, dispossession).
  • Make at least one connection to a contemporary issue or example you are familiar with.

rubric.long_description: Provides a clear, nuanced interpretation of Hofstadter’s concept of the ‘paranoid style.’ Moves beyond summary to analyze how this rhetorical pattern frames political conflict as apocalyptic and conspiratorial. Demonstrates understanding of how Hofstadter distinguishes style from clinical diagnosis.

Incorporates accurate and specific examples from Hofstadter’s essay—such as the Anti-Masons, anti-Catholic movements, Populists, or Cold War anti-Communists. Correctly identifies core features (apocalyptic stakes, hidden enemies, personalization, mountains of evidence) and explains how they function within the paranoid style.

Identifies a meaningful modern example (from any part of the political spectrum) where conspiratorial or apocalyptic rhetoric resembles Hofstadter’s paranoid style. Clearly explains the parallels without resorting to personal attacks or partisan labeling, demonstrating analytical thinking.
Uses complete sentences, coherent structure, and clear reasoning. Grammar, mechanics, and organization support the clarity of the argument. Demonstrates polish appropriate for college-level writing.
